text: Mark Fricker's quantitative work on mycelial networks provides strong evidence for functional intelligence in fungi because it shows the networks do what?
choices: Occupy a near-Pareto-optimal region of the efficiency-robustness-cost trade-off via local reinforcement and pruning
Contain a central controller that plans the entire network in advance
Grow purely at random, with no relationship to transport efficiency
Connect nodes only by the single cheapest tree, with no redundancy at all
explanation: Fricker's image analysis of real mycelia showed they reach near-Pareto-optimal solutions to the efficiency-robustness-cost trade-off through distributed local rules (reinforce high-flow cords, prune low-flow hyphae) with no central controller (choice 1). The networks are neither random (choice 2) nor a bare minimum-cost tree lacking redundancy (choice 3).
